title: Numeric Enums
definition: An Enum (Enumeration) is a feature added by TypeScript that allows you to define a set of named constants. By default, enums are number-based, starting at 0 and auto-incrementing.
simpleExplanation: Enums are like assigning human-readable names to confusing numbers. Instead of trying to remember that User Role `1` is Admin and `2` is Guest, you create an Enum. In your code you just type `Role.Admin`, and TS translates it to `1` under the hood.
realWorldExample: Handling directional movement in a game (`Direction.Up`, `Direction.Down`) or API status codes (`Status.Success`, `Status.NotFound`).

basic: What value does the first item in a numeric enum have if unassigned?
intermediate: Can you assign a custom number to start the incrementing?
advanced: What is Reverse Mapping in numeric enums?

answers.question: Can you assign a custom number?
answers.answer: Yes. If you do `enum Role { Admin = 5, Guest }`, Guest will automatically become `6`.

answers.question: What is Reverse Mapping?
answers.answer: Unlike normal objects, numeric enums compile into a two-way mapping in JavaScript. If `Direction.Up` equals `1`, then `Direction[1]` evaluates back to the string `'Up'`.
